results.name: expectedThresholdQalyLoss
results.source: integral of thresholdQalyLoss over the deployed population
results.note: the predicted side integrates the analytic accounting; the measured side draws events and books realised QALYs, so the two are different computations rather than the same one twice
results.regime: liability-threshold DGP: standard normal liability, score explaining 0.30 of it on the liability scale, disease when the liability clears the prevalence threshold; 400000 individuals per block, 8 blocks. The deployed model is miscalibrated by an intercept SHIFT on the log-odds scale. Treatment when the decision risk exceeds 0.10; benefit 0.35 QALYs on an event, harm 0.02 QALYs on everyone treated. THE MEASURED SIDE DRAWS THE ACTUAL EVENT and books realised QALYs under the oracle and deployed rules; it never evaluates the analytic loss. The estimand is the MEAN OVER INDIVIDUALS of the realised QALY difference, unweighted, matched by an unweighted mean of the predicted per-individual losses -- not a per-decision or per-event mean, which differ. Cells admitted only where the predicted loss clears three Monte-Carlo floors; excluded cells are printed

results.name: expectedThresholdQalyLoss [benefit priced at the PREDICTED risk rather than the true one, competing]
results.source: same integral with benefit * predictedRisk in the gain
results.note: the quantity a deployer actually holds, and the natural confusion; it prices the benefit at the number that is wrong; positive control 'event rate vs mean p_true at prev=0.05 shift=0.50' passed at 0.60 sems

results.name: expectedThresholdQalyLoss [benefit and harm booked together only on events, competing]
results.source: same integral with (benefit - harm) * trueRisk in the gain
results.note: charges the harm only to treated cases rather than to everyone treated, which is the other available mis-accounting; positive control 'event rate vs mean p_true at prev=0.05 shift=0.50' passed at 0.60 sems
